transcript.text: Sometimes when I open the dishwasher there's grey smelly water in the bottom even though it finished draining fine. Not every day though. Kitchen sink was replaced last month if that matters.

That grey smelly water usually means a small amount of dirty water is being left behind in the bottom of the machine after the cycle ends. To narrow this down, please switch off and unplug the dishwasher first. Then take out the lower rack, twist and lift out the filter at the bottom of the tub, rinse it under the tap, and clear any debris from the sump underneath. Let me know if you found a blockage there or if everything looked clean.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]

I've taken the filter out and it's clean, nothing in the sump either. The dishwasher drains fully at the end of the cycle, it's only later that the dirty water shows up. It seems to happen after I drain the sink full of washing-up water.

The fact that this happens specifically after you drain a lot of water from the sink strongly suggests backflow. When the sink drains quickly, dirty water can be pushed up into your dishwasher if there is no check valve to stop it. This often happens on new installations because the connection point where the dishwasher hose joins the sink waste has a small blanking plug inside it. If this plug wasn't removed or cut out when the sink was fitted, it blocks the flow from the sink and forces dirty water back into your machine instead of down the drain. Could you please check under the sink where the dishwasher hose connects to the waste pipe? Is there a small blanking plug still in place inside that connection?
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

I had a look under the sink. Since the new sink went in, the drain hose just lies on the cupboard floor and goes straight into the waste spigot, with no high loop. I haven't checked for a blanking plug inside the spigot though. Is that the likely cause?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, that is almost certainly the cause. When a new sink waste is fitted, it often comes with a small plastic blanking plug inside the spigot where hoses connect. If this wasn't removed (usually by cutting it out), water from your washing-up can't go down the drain properly and gets forced back up into your dishwasher instead. The fact that your hose lies flat on the floor without a 'high loop' makes this even more likely, as there is no physical barrier to stop that dirty water flowing backwards. Please check under the sink: shine a torch into the spigot where the grey hose enters. If you see a white or black plastic plug inside, you will need to remove it (usually by cutting it out with a utility knife). Once cleared, try running the sink and watching if the dishwasher backs up. To confirm this is the only issue and check for any safety recalls on your specific machine, could you please tell me the make and model number? It is usually on a sticker on the side edge of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint HFC 3C26 W. I'll have a look in the spigot with a torch now and let you know what I find.

That sounds like a good plan. The most common cause for this specific issue on new installations is indeed a small plastic blanking plug left inside the sink waste spigot; if it's there, it blocks the sink drain and forces dirty water back into your dishwasher when you run the washing-up. Once you've checked that, please also make sure to lift the grey drain hose up so it forms a 'high loop' (tied to the underside of the worktop or the top of the waste pipe) before it drops down into the spigot—this prevents any backflow even if the plug is removed. Let me know what you find in the spigot.

I wasn't sure what I was looking at in the spigot, so I can't say about a plug. I did loop the hose up high and clip it, though, and I've had no more water in the dishwasher since. The sink also drains a little slow, if that matters.

That is excellent news. The high loop you created has acted as a physical barrier to stop the dirty water from flowing back into your machine when the sink drains. Regarding the slow drainage in the sink itself: this suggests there may still be some debris or grease building up in the pipes, or that small blanking plug I mentioned earlier is partially blocking the spigot. While it hasn't caused a backup yet, it is worth clearing out to prevent future issues. You can try pouring a kettle of boiling water down the sink drain or using a plunger to dislodge any blockage. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
